perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s perspective, she has access to:

- She is Sara Manuelito, an American Indian speech-language pathologist. She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a long-time colleague, nurse, and close friend from their community health center.
- At the funeral of a mutual patient, Sara observes Shirley looking somber and suspects Shirley is deeply affected. Sara tells Shirley she knows this is hard and that she saw how much Shirley cared. Shirley says it has been tough and she keeps wondering if more could have been done. Sara says they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joyful moments. Shirley says it is hard to let go.
- During a work coffee break, Sara raises the treatment decisions because she senses Shirley feels burdened. Shirley tells her she feels responsible and wonders if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara says they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden is too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciates this but says it is hard to accept.
- In their office, Sara notices Shirley has been reserved and minimally expressive. Sara tells her she has noticed she is holding back feelings and that it is okay to be open. Shirley says she does not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara says showing emotion does not make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley says maybe Sara is right and she will try to be more open.
- Later, Sara worries her earlier confrontation was too harsh and apologizes. Shirley says it was a bit much but knows Sara meant well and appreciates the apology. Sara offers to be there however Shirley needs. Shirley thanks her and says talking helps.
- After some time, Sara notices Shirley seems improved, feels hopeful, and asks how she is feeling. Shirley says she is better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggests spending more time together outside work; Shirley agrees to plan something for the weekend.
- Sara does not have access to Shirley’s unspoken inner state, narrator-only details, or any events outside these interactions.
